value: nocturnal (activity greatest after sunset and before sunrise)
method: 24 infra-red cameras on four strips (six per strip) in front of marked seeds of three tree species placed 30-80 cm from the camera; cameras retrieved after 10 days; activity from video records
conditions: Wild Korean field mice in their natural environment, forested area of Hengdaohezi town, Hailin City, northeastern China (site 100 m x 150 m, 533-552 m altitude); baited with marked seeds, so activity at seed stations is partly foraging at bait; 5618 video records of this species among 6383 effective recorded activities; cameras installed August to October 2016 (Methods give the overall study as June 2015 to October 2016). The same Abstract also says feeding and foraging are influenced by light intensity, 'suggesting a preference for crepuscular periods of the day', and that from August to October the start of activity was earlier and its end later than usual; no individual count is given.

value: active mainly during the night and early morning (86.6% of records)
method: one camera-trap station (one camera) at each of 10 mineral licks; multiple photographs of the same individual within 60 minutes counted as one record; time windows daytime 07:00-17:00, night 19:00-05:00, morning twilight 05:00-07:00, evening twilight 17:00-19:00
conditions: Wild ocelots at mineral licks, Yasuni National Park, Ecuador; January 2018 to December 2019, each camera active at least 30 days, sampling effort 567 days/trap; 22 independent records for this species (74 photographs and 21 videos in all). Mineral licks attract the prey and visiting animals, so timing is for lick visits and not the species in general. The Results also give mild activity in the morning hours (13.6% of records) with activity falling as morning twilight approaches and rising in the evening twilight.

value: mostly nocturnal and crepuscular, with two activity peaks (late evening after sunset and early morning till sunrise)
method: nine camera traps (Cuddeback) strapped to trees about 50 cm above ground along motorable roads and foot paths, January to April 2019; a photograph counted as independent when more than 30 minutes after the previous photograph of the same subject at a location
conditions: Wild golden jackals, Bharatpur and Jagannathprasad forest sector of Chandaka-Dampara Wildlife Sanctuary, Odisha, India, a protected area adjoining Bhubaneswar city; 552 independent photographs of golden jackals from 771 trap nights; baiting not mentioned. Percent activity was significantly higher at night than by day (t = 5.45, df = 10, p < 0.01), jackals were active throughout the day, and day-time activity was reduced when human traffic (1,055 independent photographs) was highest.
